## Standing instruction: congruence proofs (keywords: congruence, SSS, SAS, ASA, proof outline, diagrams)
- User (June 2024) asked: always give detailed proof outlines WITH diagrams whenever they ask about triangle congruence criteria (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS).
- Format that worked: label vertices in matching order; mark given parts on ASCII diagram; choose criterion by checking "included" position; two-column Statement | Reason table; conclude with criterion name.
- Always flag SSA (not valid) and AAA (similarity only) when relevant.

## User preferences (keywords: diagram, visual, triangle classification, learning style)
- Christina (colour technologist, learning triangle geometry, prefers visual learning).
- Standing request: when asking about triangle classification methods, always give step-by-step geometric diagrams (ASCII is fine).
- Her notes say she gets triangle classification mostly right (15 problems, >80%), she's working on Law of Cosines, Triangle Sum Theorem, Pythagorean theorem.

## Standing instruction: triangle area answers (keywords: area, comparative analysis, solution methods)
- When asked about triangle area calculations, always include a comparative analysis of multiple solution methods (e.g., base-height, Heron's, shoelace/coordinates, trig ½ab·sinC), stating which is most efficient for the given data.
